mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations through increased discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals a tight labor market that may trigger inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., when both series decline, SPX 60-day returns are positive in >40% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations through increased discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110 indicates a contraction in the manufacturing sector, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO is below 110.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is above 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates an inflationary monetary tightening cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., when both series rise, SPX 60-day returns are positive in >40% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS is rising.
